tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README and CLAUDE.md to understand what iptvchannels is: an IPTV channel manager that exports Home Assistant YAML and M3U playlists, backed by TanStack Start + Drizzle ORM + Supabase.
tour.languageLesson: CLAUDE.md is an "AI context file" — a project-specific brief that gives assistants the authoritative architecture, patterns, and gotchas before they touch code.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap & Routing
tour.description: See how the app boots: router.tsx builds the TanStack Router with React Query SSR integration and custom array-based search serialization, while __root.tsx provides the SSR document shell every route renders into.

tour.title: Home & System Map
tour.description: The home page explains the navigation and how channels, movies, series, Kodi sync, and the M3U/YAML feeds fit together — a guided map of the whole system.

tour.title: The Data Model
tour.description: The heart of the system: the Drizzle schema defines the normalized group_titles lookup shared by channels, media, and series via foreign keys — changing a group alias propagates to every linked row.
tour.languageLesson: Normalizing a free-text field (group_title) into its own lookup table is the pattern that lets one alias edit update hundreds of rows — a classic foreign-key tradeoff.

tour.title: DB Client & Validation
tour.description: src/db/index.ts lazily initializes the Drizzle client behind a Proxy so the module is safe to import in SSR/client contexts, and validators.ts holds the Zod schemas plus the ISO country-code list.

tour.title: The Shared Server Engine
tour.description: shared.ts is the generic engine behind channels, movies, and series: paginated queries, CRUD logic, and group-title FK upsert — one stream abstraction serving three resource types.

tour.title: Server Functions & API Routes
tour.description: These createServerFn wrappers expose CRUD and exports; src/server.ts registers the /channels/m3u, /movies/m3u, and /channels/yaml API routes served by Nitro.

tour.title: The Channels Page
tour.description: The channels page wires server-filtered pagination with group/country/active filters and export actions; ListStream renders the rows and ActiveSwitch performs optimistic active-state toggles via React Query.

tour.title: Forms & Validation
tour.description: The resource forms bind to the Zod validators, resolving group titles and country codes; SeriesForm adds dynamic episode rows for series-with-episodes management.

tour.title: M3U Pipeline — Parse & Export
tour.description: Trace the M3U lifecycle: parseM3uContent ingests seed files (splitting live channels vs movies/series), and generateM3u emits active rows back as a playlist served by the m3u server function.

tour.title: Home Assistant YAML Export
tour.description: generateHomeAssistantYaml emits the plain top-level script mapping (no script: wrapper) meant for !include; the YAML endpoint runs a Kodi sync first and prefixes a stats/skip-reason header.

tour.title: Kodi Sync Integration
tour.description: runKodiSync queries Kodi JSON-RPC PVR.GetChannels, matchKodiChannels resolves labels by name then tvg_name (case-insensitive), and only content_id is written back — feeding the YAML export.

tour.title: Shared UI Package
tour.description: The @iptvchannels/ui workspace: cn() merges Tailwind classes and the shadcn/ui components (Button, Select, …) form the consistent design system used across every form and list.

tour.title: Database Scripts & Migrations
tour.description: How data gets in: seed-channels.sh imports M3U via PostgreSQL COPY with a staging-table + FK-join pattern, the SQL migrations establish the normalized schema, and drizzle.config.ts drives env-aware schema pushes.
